title: Read pane text only when the heartbeat is already stale, not on every poll tick
action: Per D4, slice 3 of the plan — the follow-up hlp-1's own cap already flagged ('pane_read polled every tick rather than only on stale heartbeat'). Today the production tick closure in wait_for_round calls herdr.pane_read(pane_id) on EVERY 200ms tick and hands the text to decide_poll, but decide_poll consumes pane_text ONLY inside its stale-heartbeat branch. At the 900s idle timeout that is roughly 4,500 discarded subprocess spawns per worker per stall. TAKE THE SEAM THAT DOES NOT TOUCH decide_poll: change run_poll_loop's `tick` parameter from `impl FnMut() -> PollTick` to `impl FnMut(bool) -> PollTick`, where the bool is `heartbeat_already_stale` — computed in run_poll_loop from the same `now - last_heartbeat_ms >= idle_timeout` expression decide_poll uses, evaluated BEFORE the tick so the closure knows whether the text will be needed. The production closure calls herdr.pane_read(pane_id).ok() only when that flag is true, and passes pane_text: None otherwise. decide_poll's signature, body, branch order and ALL SEVEN of its existing tests stay completely untouched — that is the point of choosing this seam. The three existing run_poll_loop tests and any other closure sites gain an ignored parameter (|_| ...) with NO change to any expected value. Watch the boundary case: on the exact tick where staleness first becomes true the flag must already be true, so paused_limit still fires on the same tick it fires today — the existing FakeHerdr end-to-end tests (stale_heartbeat_with_matching_pane_text_pauses_limit..., stale_heartbeat_with_non_matching_pane_text_times_out_idle_unchanged, fresh_heartbeat_with_matching_pane_text_keeps_waiting_until_result_ready) must pass byte-identically. Add one test proving pane_read is NOT called while the heartbeat is fresh: script FakeHerdr to count pane_read calls and assert the count stays zero across several fresh-heartbeat ticks, then becomes non-zero once the heartbeat goes stale. Do not touch the tier-1 liveness cadence (every 10th tick), the debounce, or anything else from hls-1.

truths: pane_read is not called on a tick whose heartbeat is fresh, proven by a call-counting fake
paused_limit and timed_out_idle still fire on exactly the tick they fire today — the three existing FakeHerdr classification tests pass with no assertion changed
decide_poll's signature, body and all seven of its existing tests are untouched
The tier-1 liveness cadence and debounce from hls-1 are unchanged

trace.outcome: A stall now costs one pane read instead of roughly 4500 discarded subprocess spawns

checks.evidence: run.rs wait_for_round closure now guards the read: pane_text = if heartbeat_already_stale { herdr.pane_read(pane_id).ok() } else { None }. Pinned by pane_read_is_not_called_while_heartbeat_is_fresh_and_polled_when_stale, which asserts the call-counting fake records exactly one read for a whole stall and that it names the right pane

heartbeat_already_stale is computed in run_poll_loop from the SAME expression decide_poll uses (now - last_heartbeat >= idle_timeout * 1000). Orchestrator traced the one-tick skew: the flag reads last_heartbeat BEFORE this tick's freshness is applied, so it can only ever be true when decide_poll would be false (one wasted read, no verdict change) and never false when decide_poll needs the text. paused_limit and timed_out_idle therefore still fire on the tick they fire today; the three FakeHerdr classification tests are untouched by the diff
The diff contains no hunk touching decide_poll's signature, body, branch order, or any of its seven tests. The chosen seam was run_poll_loop's tick parameter, exactly so that surface stayed frozen
tick_index increment, the every-10th-tick liveness read, and the absent/unknown debounce arithmetic appear nowhere in the diff. The liveness sequence tests gained only an ignored closure parameter

Every pre-existing closure site changed only from || to |_|; no expected value changed. One existing test gained an added assertion that pane_read stays uncalled on the result-ready path — a strengthening, not a relaxation
